Results.ReviewText:
This product was fully assembled and delivered by the retail store from which it was purchased, so I cannot rate the ease of assembly.

Pros: Well constructed quality grill that meets expectations regarding performance and anticipated durability/life-span.

Cons: Expensive relative to comparable competitors products.  The top rack, which is commonly used for toasting buns, is too small so you can toast only about five buns while cooking up to 16 burgers at a time.  Not very 'mobile'... i.e. difficult to move from one location to another due to cheap plastic wheels, and folding shelve that does not allow you to simply lift and pull... difficult to tilt back on the two wheels.  You would think that after all these years someone would design a feature to include handles, quality wheels, etc... for easier movement.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I've had this grill for  two weeks, it was purchased to replace my 13 year old Weber  silverline (not sure of exact model name).  My old grill still worked but was starting to show signs of age, igniter would not light both burners.   The new Spirit II E-310 is an amazing grill, it heats up quickly, has consistent heat,  and seems to be made of high quality materials.  I bought it still in the box since a pre-assembled unit wouldn't fit in my car.  I am fairly handy with tools and found the assembly instructions excellent, the use of illustration over written instructions helped simplify assembly.  I did a lot of on-line research about all brands of grills and decided on spending the extra $ for a Weber based on two major factors: while most grills heat quickly and evenly (at least when new) it was the quality and warrantee.  Webber is the only manufacturer that is warranted  for 10 years on parts, that says a lot about what they think of the quality of their product, all other manufacturers warrantee for only 1-2 years,  which about the time most people that reviewed the other brands of grills say they needed parts replaced.  If you're considering a less expensive grill consider that you will probably be replacing parts after a season or two while the more expensive Weber will still be working  for at least ten years, or in my cast 13+ years.

The opposite side stainless steel hinged side counter isn't strong enough to lift and move forward; if attempted, it will likely break.  Hence, the only way to safely move it is to lower the side counter and place your left hand under the grill behind the left control knob and place your right hand underneath the right side of the grill.  Moving is awkward because of the relative weight of the grill and the obstructing legs in front of you as you take tiny quick steps to roll it along . . . your shins will bang into the legs. Results.ReviewText:
This grill replaced a 20+ year old Weber that would still be on my patio if a couple of the burners finall gave up to corrosion. As this grill is made in China and noticeably cheaper and lacks the rugged feel of the one it replaced. Unfortunately, this change did not result in a more cost-friendly grill.

Oddly enough, this grill has the 3 burners running fore and aft as opposed to the previous one, with burners running left and right. This after Weber touting the advantages of the fore and aft orientation.


All that aside, the grill does a nice job, even heat across the grates and easy temperature control, just not sure it is worth the extra cost compared to other grills with similar features.
